CITY OF ALHAMBRA PLANNING COMMISSION
  ACTION MINUTES

  Regular Meeting
  November 20, 2023

A.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER: 7:00 P.M. in the Council Chambers of Alhambra City Hall,
  and via video conference and teleconference.

B.  ROLL CALL:

  Present:  Bryden, Gardea, Grijalva, Ho, Juarez, Mojarro, Tsujii, Garcia

  Absent:  Pham, Olson

  Staff Present: Vanessa Reynoso, Deputy Director; Maia McCurley, Principal Planner;
  Erica Vega, Deputy City Attorney

C.  FLAG SALUTE:  Led by Vice President Garcia

D.  CONSENT AGENDA:

  AGENDA
  ITEM 1:  MINUTES – November 6, 2023 (7:01 P.M.)
  • Request: This is a request for the Planning Commission to approve
  the Minutes of the November 6, 2023, Regular Meeting of the
  Alhambra Planning Commission.
  • Recommended Action: Commission review and approve as
  submitted the Minutes of the November 6, 2023, Regular Meeting of
  the Alhambra Planning Commission.

  MOTION:
  •  Moved to approve Consent Agenda Item 1.
  •  Moved by Commissioner Bryden, Seconded by Commissioner Gardea.
  •  The motion carried by the following roll call vote:

  Roll Call Vote: 7-0-1-2
  Ayes:  Bryden, Gardea, Grijalva, Ho, Juarez, Tsujii, Garcia
  Noes:  None
  Abstain: Mojarro
  Absent: Pham, Olson

  •  For additional information regarding the discussion, the audio and video
  recordings of the discussion is available here:

E.  DISCUSSION ITEMS:

  •  There were no Discussion items.

F.  PUBLIC HEARINGS:

  AGENDA
  ITEM 2:  PLANNED DEVELOPMENT PERMIT PD-22-30 (7:02 P.M.)
  • 1624 Front Street
  • Request: This is an application for a Planned Development Permit
  PD-22-30 to demolish an existing detached two-car garage, and
  construct a 427 square foot detached two-car garage and a two-story
  1,485 square foot detached second unit to the rear of an existing 984
  square foot single-family dwelling unit on a site of approximately
  6,467 square feet located in the R-3 (Multiple Family Residential)
  zone.
  • Recommended Action: Continue the public hearing to a date
  unknown.

  MOTION:
  •  Moved to continue the public hearing to a date uncertain.
  •  Moved by Commissioner Ho, Seconded by Commissioner Tsujii.
  •  The motion carried by the following roll call vote:

  Roll Call Vote: 8-0-0-2
  Ayes:  Bryden, Gardea, Grijalva, Ho, Juarez, Mojarro, Tsujii,
  Garcia
  Noes:  None
  Abstain: None
  Absent: Pham, Olson

  AGENDA
  ITEM 3: CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT CUP-22-27 AND LOT MERGER LOTM-
  23-05 (7:02 P.M.)
  • 24 & 28 East Valley Boulevard
  • Request: This is an application for a Conditional Use Permit CUP-
  22-27 and a Lot Merger LOTM-23-05 to combine two (2) parcels into
  one (1) parcel and to establish a motor vehicle sales use within an
  existing commercial retail lease space located in the VSP (Valley
  Boulevard Corridor Specific Plan) zone.
  • Recommended Action: Continue the public hearing to a date
  unknown.

  MOTION:
  •  Moved to continue the public hearing to a date uncertain.

   •  Moved by Commissioner Ho, Seconded by Commissioner Tsujii.
  •  The motion carried by the following roll call vote:

  Roll Call Vote: 8-0-0-2
  Ayes:  Bryden, Gardea, Grijalva, Ho, Juarez, Mojarro, Tsujii,
  Garcia
  Noes:  None
  Abstain: None
  Absent: Pham, Olson

AGENDA
ITEM 4:  ZONING TEXT AMENDMENT AMD-23-11 (7:03 P.M.)
  • Citywide
  • Request: This is an application to amend the Zoning Code to allow
  medicinal cannabis delivery-only retailers in the I (Industrial) zone
  with a Conditional Use Permit and a regulatory business permit to
  implement the requirements of SB 1186.
  • Recommended Action: Adopt Resolution 23-33 recommending that
  the City Council adopt Zoning Text Amendment AMD-23-11, an
  ordinance amending the Zoning Code to allow medicinal cannabis
  delivery-only retailers in the I (Industrial) zone with a Conditional
  Use Permit and a regulatory business permit to implement the
  requirements of SB 1186, and finding Zoning Text Amendment
  AMD-23-11 to be exempt from review under the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3)
  of Title 14 of the California Code of Regulations, which exempts from
  CEQA review projects that have no possibility of causing a significant
  effect on the environment.
  • Deputy City Attorney Erica Vega provided the Staff presentation.
  • The public hearing was opened and then closed.

MOTION:
  •  Moved to approve with three (3) amendments to be incorporated into the
  proposed ordinance: 1.) Only businesses with Type 9-M licenses shall be
  permitted; 2.) Businesses shall be at least 600’ from residential zones; and
  3.) Businesses shall be at least 600’ from businesses that are conditionally
  permitted and primarily focused on providing services to children.
  •  Moved by Commissioner Gardea, Seconded by Commissioner Tsujii.
  •  The motion carried by the following roll call vote:

  Roll Call Vote: 8-0-0-2
  Ayes:  Bryden, Gardea, Grijalva, Ho, Juarez, Mojarro, Tsujii,
  Garcia
  Noes:  None
  Abstain: None
  Absent: Pham, Olson
